issues.basis: NL2 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected'; FCSTM complete transition inventory (7 transitions, none targeting the composite from outside); inspection_equivalent_facts reachability showing Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts reachability refutation for state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5; working_contract showing UnspecifiedInitial as compiler_owned synthetic_state with no outgoing transitions.
issues.expected: A transition exists from the state preceding collision avoidance activation into the Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode composite, triggered by collision detection events, enabling the sub-machine to become active.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory contains 7 transitions. None targets Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode. The only root-level transition is [*] to UnspecifiedInitial (line:19). UnspecifiedInitial has zero outgoing transitions. All transitions involving the composite are internal to its scope (region initial entries and final exits). The composite is unreachable from the top-level initial entry per verify_facts reachability refutation.
issues.reason: The NL contract requires a transition that activates (enters) the collision avoidance sub-machine from a preceding state. The complete closed transition inventory (7 edges) contains no edge targeting Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode from any external source. The only root-level state (UnspecifiedInitial) is a compiler synthetic with no outgoing edges. This is a clear structural absence: the activation transition described by NL does not exist in the model.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML author may have intended the composite to be the top-level state of the diagram (i.e., the diagram IS the sub-machine), making the 'activation from an external state' a context-level concern not expressible within this single diagram. The -- separators and internal [*] transitions could be read as the activation mechanism within the diagram's own scope. However, the NL explicitly says 'becomes active when... detected,' implying a prior non-active state, and the model provides no such prior authored state with an outgoing transition to the composite.
issues.title: No transition exists from root-level state into Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode composite

issues.basis: NL2 naming three collision types; FCSTM events inventory showing only collision_detected and Collision_avoided; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers showing collision_detected consumers at transitions line:12/14/16 (all internal to composite) with reachable_consumer_transition_refs empty; verify_facts event-consumer:collision_detected refuted; UnspecifiedInitial outgoing_transition_refs empty; source_inventory events ['collision detected', 'Collision avoided'] confirming only one collision event in author source.
issues.expected: Each of the three collision detection events (frontend collision detected, rear-end collision detected, collision with pedestrian detected) must be consumable in the state preceding collision avoidance activation, with transitions from that state triggered by these events entering the sub-machine.
issues.observed: The model declares only one event (collision_detected, named 'collision detected'), not three distinct events. This single event's consumers are transitions line:12, 14, 16, all within the Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode scope (region initial entries). The state preceding activation (UnspecifiedInitial) has zero outgoing transitions and consumes no events. verify_facts confirms event-consumer:collision_detected is refuted with reachable_consumer_transition_refs empty. The EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic confirms no consumer is reachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The contract requires three collision events to be consumable from the 'state preceding collision avoidance activation.' The model fails this in two ways: (1) only one generic event exists instead of three distinct ones, and (2) that event is consumed only within the composite (by conditional initial entries in each region), not from the external preceding state which has no transitions at all. The event_consumer_coverage property is violated because no consumer of the collision events exists in the required scope.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL may use 'frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian' as descriptive labels for three scenarios of a single 'collision detected' event rather than requiring three distinct event declarations. The three regions (F, R, P) distinguish the collision type structurally rather than through separate events. However, the contract explicitly names three events and requires them to be consumable from the preceding state, which the model does not support regardless of event naming interpretation.
issues.title: Collision detection events are not consumable from the state preceding sub-machine activation

issues.basis: NL2 'becomes active when... detected'; FCSTM transitions line:12/14/16 all with triggers=[collision_detected]; reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING (composite_path=llms_emp_feedback_final_0017.Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, existing_conditional_count=3); verify_facts initial-entry refutations for line:12/14/16 (has_trigger=true); inspection_equivalent_facts INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics at lines 12, 14, 16; PlantUML showing all three region entries as [*] --> X : collision detected.
issues.expected: The composite Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode has at least one unconditional initial entry transition (from [*] to a child state with no trigger) so that each concurrent region has a well-defined initial state upon activation, consistent with UML orthogonal region semantics.
issues.observed: All three initial pseudostate transitions within the composite (line:12 [*] to F, line:14 [*] to R, line:16 [*] to P) carry the trigger collision_detected. No unconditional initial entry exists. The reference_inspection_facts W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING diagnostic confirms existing_conditional_count=3 with no unconditional fallback. verify_facts refutes initial-entry for all three transitions (has_trigger=true for each). The INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics at lines 12, 14, 16 in inspection_equivalent_facts independently confirm the conditional nature.
issues.reason: The NL establishes that the sub-machine 'becomes active when... collision... is detected.' For a composite with orthogonal (concurrent) regions, activation requires each region to have a defined initial state. The model provides only conditional initial entries, meaning no region has a defined state if the composite is entered without the collision_detected trigger firing. This is a structural defect in the region initial entry mechanism, distinct from the missing external activation transition (REF-002) and the event consumer coverage gap (REF-005). The derived contract captures this independent initial_entry property.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The author may have intentionally made all region entries conditional on collision_detected to express that each region only activates its collision state when that specific event occurs, treating the composite's activation as implicit. In this reading, the 'initial entry' is the conditional entry itself, and the empty region 0 serves as a default 'inactive' state. However, UML concurrent region semantics require each region to have exactly one initial pseudostate transition that is unconditional (or at least has a defined default); purely conditional entries leave the region's initial state undefined if the trigger does not fire.
issues.title: Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode lacks an unconditional initial entry for its concurrent regions

issues.basis: NL2 segment; complete FCSTM transition inventory (7 transitions: lines 19,12,13,14,15,16,17) - none has target=Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode with source outside its scope; verify_facts reachability:state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5 refuted; inspection_facts STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for line 5; PlantUML source shows no transition entering the composite from outside
issues.expected: A transition from the state preceding activation to Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, triggered by collision detection, exists in the closed model.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory contains 7 transitions; none targets Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode from any external state. The composite has zero incoming edges from the root scope. Its only incoming transitions are internal initial-pseudostate edges (line 12, 14, 16) within its own scope.
issues.reason: The contract requires a transition with source='state preceding collision avoidance activation' and target='collision avoidance sub-machine'. The target is exactly bound to state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5. The source is ambiguous (no author-defined external state exists). The complete transition inventory confirms no edge targets the composite from outside. Predicate S2 requires both exact source and target; since the source cannot be uniquely bound, predicate_id=null. The absence is an exact negative inventory result, not a binding failure.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL's 'activates the sub-machine' could refer to the internal initial entry transitions ([*] to F/R/P) within the composite rather than an external transition entering it. In that reading, the sub-machine is 'activated' by its own initial transitions firing, and no external edge is required. The PlantUML shows Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode as the top-level state with no outer context, supporting the interpretation that its internal initial entries constitute its activation.
issues.title: No transition enters Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode from root scope

issues.basis: NL2 establishes Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode as a required operating sub-machine; verify_facts reachability:state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5 status=refuted finite_scope=closed_fcstm_hierarchy; inspection_facts reachable_state_refs=[state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0017:line:1, state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:4]; transition:line:19 source=[*] target=UnspecifiedInitial scope=llms_emp_feedback_final_0017 triggers=[]; UnspecifiedInitial outgoing_transition_refs=[]; all 6 verify_facts reachability checks for descendants also refuted
issues.expected: A finite path exists from the model root to Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, making the required operating sub-machine behaviorally accessible.
issues.observed: No path exists from root to Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode. The root's sole initial edge (transition:line:19) targets UnspecifiedInitial (a compiler-synthetic state with zero outgoing transitions). The reachable set from root is exactly {root, UnspecifiedInitial}. All 7 states within or under Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode are confirmed unreachable by verify_facts.
issues.reason: The verify_facts provide a deterministically refuted reachability check: no finite path from root to Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode exists in the closed FCSTM hierarchy. The root's initial edge goes to UnspecifiedInitial (synthetic, no outgoing), creating a top-level behavioral dead-end. This means the required operating sub-machine can never be entered, making all its internal behavior (activation, collision handling, completion) operationally impossible. G1 (path-existence) is the appropriate frozen predicate for this finite reachability claim.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode is the author's top-level state in the PlantUML; the root wrapper llms_emp_feedback_final_0017 is a compiler artifact added during FCSTM lowering. The unreachability is a consequence of the compiler's lowering strategy (creating a synthetic initial target instead of wiring the root's initial edge to the author's top-level composite), not an author modeling error. A faithful lowering would have connected [*] directly to Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode.
issues.title: Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode unreachable from model root

issues.basis: NL2 establishes three collision detection events as activation triggers requiring consumability in the pre-activation state; inspection_facts event_consumers collision_detected: consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:12, transition:line:14, transition:line:16], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; verify_facts event-consumer:collision_detected status=refuted reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; all three consumer transitions have scope=Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode with reachable_from_initial=false; no transition in root scope (llms_emp_feedback_final_0017) has collision_detected in its triggers
issues.expected: Each collision detection event must be consumable in the state preceding collision avoidance activation; at least one consumer transition for the event must be reachable from the model root.
issues.observed: Event collision_detected has 3 declared consumer transitions (line 12 to F, line 14 to R, line 16 to P) but 0 reachable consumers. All consumers are scoped inside Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode, which is unreachable from root. The verify_facts event-consumer check for collision_detected is refuted with reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]. No transition in the root scope consumes collision_detected.
issues.reason: The contract requires each collision detection event to be consumable in the pre-activation state. The deterministic event_consumer_fact shows collision_detected has declared consumers (3 transitions) but zero reachable consumers. The verify_facts confirm with a refuted event-consumer check. The behavioral consequence is that no collision detection event can ever trigger any response in the closed model - the events are effectively unconsumed at the operational level. No frozen predicate directly expresses 'event has at least one reachable consumer in scope,' so predicate_id=null.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three NL collision types are collapsed into a single model event collision_detected, which is a faithful simplification since the NL uses 'or' (any collision type triggers activation). The event IS consumed (transitions exist); the issue is purely that the composite containing the consumers is unreachable due to the root's defective initial entry. If the root's initial edge targeted Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode instead of UnspecifiedInitial, the event consumers would become reachable and this contract would be satisfied. The event-consumer wiring within the composite is correct; the defect is upstream.
issues.title: Collision detection events have no reachable consumers in the pre-activation scope

decisions.reason: The NL2 language 'This sub-machine becomes active when... detected' establishes a primary reading that an activation transition is required. The complete transition inventory confirms no such transition exists. However, the source structure (composite as top-level state with no outer scope) supports an alternative reading where the diagram is the sub-machine itself and activation is an external concern. Both readings are compatible with the supplied facts: the NL does not explicitly say 'a transition from state X enters the sub-machine' and the model does not contain an outer context. The compiler-synthetic UnspecifiedInitial (confirmed by working_contract) further supports that no author-intended pre-activation state exists in the diagram.

The diagram may represent the sub-machine in isolation, making 'becomes active when detected' a context-level description of how the sub-machine is entered from outside this diagram, not a requirement for an explicit external transition within the diagram.

However, the NL2 language 'becomes active when... detected' supports an alternative reading where the conditional entries are the intentional activation mechanism: the regions do not need a pre-activation 'idle' state because the composite is only entered when the detection event is present. This reading is compatible with the supplied facts (the NL does not explicitly require an unconditional initial state; it requires activation upon detection, which the conditional entries implement). The UML invariant violations for each specific transition are captured separately in obligations i8, i9, i10.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The author may have intentionally made all region entries conditional on collision_detected to express that each region activates its collision state only when the detection event occurs, treating the composite's external activation as implicit. In this reading, the conditional entries ARE the activation mechanism: when the composite is entered (from external context) with the collision_detected event, each region's initial entry fires and directs to the appropriate state. The NL 'becomes active when... detected' is implemented by this conditional entry mechanism rather than by a separate unconditional initial state plus a triggered transition.

All three region initial entries (line 12, 14, 16) are conditional on collision_detected.

candidate.expected: The composite Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode has at least one unconditional initial entry transition (from [*] to a child state with no trigger) so that each concurrent region has a well-defined initial state upon activation, consistent with UML orthogonal region semantics.
candidate.observed: All three initial pseudostate transitions within the composite (line:12 [*] to F, line:14 [*] to R, line:16 [*] to P) carry the trigger collision_detected. candidate.reason: The NL establishes that the sub-machine 'becomes active when... collision... is detected.' For a composite with orthogonal (concurrent) regions, activation requires each region to have a defined initial state. The model provides only conditional initial entries, meaning no region has a defined state if the composite is entered without the collision_detected trigger firing. This is a structural defect in the region initial entry mechanism, distinct from the missing external activation transition (REF-002) and the event consumer coverage gap (REF-005). candidate.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.

In this reading, the 'initial entry' is the conditional entry itself, and the empty region 0 serves as a default 'inactive' state. However, UML concurrent region semantics require each region to have exactly one initial pseudostate transition that is unconditional (or at least has a defined default); purely conditional entries leave the region's initial state undefined if the trigger does not fire.
